chunks: And by this chain, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you are in a row, greet with a greeting to your right and a greeting to your left, because on your left is the one who greets you; and when you are the Imam, greet with one greeting while you are facing the Qiblah.'
ai.seo_question: How does the greeting (Salām) differ for the Imam versus the follower in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the procedural nuances of the final greeting (*Taslim*) in prayer, distinguishing between the congregant who greets both sides to acknowledge fellow worshippers and the Imam who faces the Qiblah for a single, unified greeting. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the distinct roles within the prayer formation (*Saff*), ensuring that the ritual maintains both communal cohesion and directional integrity as prescribed by Imam al-Sadiq.
